segments.contextAfter: `reply`: A block or closure to indicate success or failure. If activation succeeds, pass the root [`FSItem`](fsitem.md) and a `nil` error. If activation fails, pass the relevant error as the second parameter; FSKit ignores any [`FSItem`](fsitem.md) in this case. In Swift, `reply` takes only the [`FSItem`](fsitem.md) as the parameter; you signal any error with a `throw`. For an `async` Swift implementation, there’s no reply handler; simply return the [`FSItem`](fsitem.md) or throw an error.
